belief: My worth depends on how much I serve.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that your worth depends on how much you serve, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Being praised mainly for being helpful or useful as a child. A church culture that celebrated the busiest volunteers. Feeling valuable only when needed. Trouble saying no. Guilt when resting or when others serve you.
teaches: Your worth comes from God’s love, not your usefulness. God tells His people that they are precious and honored in His sight, and that He loves them. When Martha was busy serving and Mary sat at Jesus’ feet, Jesus said Mary had chosen the good portion. Service matters: we are created in Christ to do good works. But we serve because we are loved and valuable, not to become loved and valuable.
self_statements: I’m only valuable when I’m helping.
If I stop serving, no one will want me.
I have to say yes to every request.
God loves people who do more for Him.
errors: Believing your value depends on what you do.
“I should always be available to serve.”
Calling yourself “useless” when you are not serving.
Believing you must serve constantly or be worthless.
questions: What does God say about my worth in Isaiah 43:4?
Why did Jesus say Mary chose the better portion?
Am I serving from love or from fear of being worthless?
Did Jesus ever rest or tell His disciples to rest?
Would I still be loved by God if I could never serve again?
Who taught me that my worth comes from being useful?
What would healthy service look like for me?
truth: My worth does not depend on how much I serve. I am precious and honored in God’s sight because He loves me. Jesus values time with Him more than busyness for Him. I can serve out of love and gratitude, and I can also rest, say no, and let others serve me.
hw_questions: What does God say about my worth?
Why did Mary choose the better portion?
Am I serving from love or fear?
Did Jesus rest and tell others to rest?
Would God love me if I could never serve again?
What does healthy service look like?
hw_truths: I am precious and honored in God’s sight.
My worth comes from God’s love, not my usefulness.
Time with Jesus matters more than busyness for Him.
I serve because I am loved, not to be loved.
Jesus’ yoke is easy and His burden is light.
log: Each day, write one way God showed He loves me that had nothing to do with what I did.
name_example: Because Sarah is precious and honored in My sight, and because I love her, I will give men in exchange for her and nations in place of her life.
actions: Say no to one request this week
kindly, and notice what actually happens.
Spend twenty minutes simply sitting with Jesus,
reading Scripture or praying, without a to-do list.
without arguing or paying them back.
and write what Jesus valued most.
tracker: One time I rested or said no
prayer: Father, thank You that I am precious and honored in Your sight because You love me. Help me reject the lie that my worth depends on how much I serve. Teach me to sit at Jesus’ feet, to rest without guilt, and to serve out of love and gratitude. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
songs: Our identity comes from being God's child, freely chosen and set free, not from what we produce.
Sets God's view of us against the voices that say we are not enough.
We are God's beloved children because of His love, not because of how much we do for Him.
A joyful reminder that grace, not our effort or service, is what holds us and makes us God's.
